newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Pena sees progress in Russian nuclear stocks safety.
newsitem.headline: Pena sees progress in Russian nuclear stocks safety.

text.p: U.S. Energy Secretary Federico Pena said on Wednesday that U.S. efforts to help Russia keep its huge stockpiles of nuclear materials safe were working.
"Today, I'm pleased to announce that this co-operation effort is growing," he told a news conference, adding later, "in short, we're making progress."

Pena met Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov, who is also energy minister, Nuclear Energy Minister Viktor Mikhailov and others on a first visit to Russia, where nuclear security issues topped his agenda.

"Russia and the United States have the world's largest stockpile of nuclear weapons and weapons-grade materials, and we share the belief, formalised through a number of agreements, that these dangerous weapons and materials must not fall into the wrong hands," Pena said.
Russia's nuclear sector, once the pride of Soviet science, is in financial crisis and workers have in the past protested against wage arrears.
Washington and some other Western countries, notably Germany, have expressed concerns that materials may leak out of the country.

Pena and Mikhailov signed an agreement earlier this week to include one more Russian nuclear research institute, known as Lytkarino, in a programme to account for, control and protect Russian nuclear materials.
Pena said additional agreements could be announced in September when senior Russian officials meet their U.S. counterparts.

Russia has been installing sensors, monitors, radiation-detection equipment and security devices at various facilities, and Pena said the moves were occuring at an important time, as Russia undertakes to transform its old economy.
He said he had discussed with officials stopping production of weapons-grade nuclear materials not required for military purposes at three reactors, in Tomsk and Krasnoyarsk.
